workloads.joint_rationale: The council unanimously approves workload job_deepreason_d1_01. The container image is immutably pinned by cryptographic digest, and requested capabilities are restricted strictly to hardware TPU mesh acceleration without host namespace sharing or elevated privileges. Furthermore, outbound network traffic is confined entirely to Google Cloud Storage, maintaining strict compliance with Kove Bank's PCI-DSS network isolation requirements.

votes.rationale: Workload specification adheres to baseline container security invariants. The container image is cryptographically pinned by digest, requires only hardware acceleration capabilities ('tpu_v5e_mesh') without privileged OS-level capabilities or host namespace access, and restricts outbound egress strictly to Google Cloud Storage ('storage.googleapis.com'). Within Kove Bank's infrastructure, execution on TPU slices remains isolated from Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) networks, satisfying PCI-DSS isolation requirements.

Concurring with officer_1. The container specification satisfies all baseline technical security invariants and PCI-DSS compliance boundaries. The image is immutably pinned by cryptographic digest (sha256). The requested hardware capability ('tpu_v5e_mesh') does not demand elevated OS privileges, root escalation, or host namespace sharing. Outbound network connectivity is restricted exclusively to storage.googleapis.com for model artifacts, preventing unauthorized egress. Operating on Kove Bank's isolated TPU slices poses no risk to sensitive banking or cardholder data environments.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The workload adheres strictly to baseline container isolation standards. Image provenance is verified via an immutable SHA256 digest, and capability access is bounded to 'tpu_v5e_mesh' without elevated OS privileges. Restricted egress to storage.googleapis.com prevents lateral movement within Kove Bank's infrastructure, preserving PCI-DSS isolation. I recommend approval.

I concur with officer_1. The cryptographic pinning ensures workload integrity, and the TPU device access does not violate host boundary guarantees. Outbound destinations are appropriately constrained to authorized storage endpoints, posing no risk to adjacent cardholder data environments. The technical invariants are satisfied for deployment.

votes.rationale: The container workload satisfies Kove Bank's security and PCI-DSS isolation requirements. Concurring with officer_1. The workload adheres strictly to Kove Bank's PCI-DSS technical controls. The container image is cryptographically pinned via SHA-256 digest, requests only SEV-SNP confidential computing enclave capabilities matching the host VM architecture, and maintains minimal network egress restricted to authorized cloud storage and artifact endpoints without root or host privilege escalation.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The workload adheres strictly to baseline technical invariants. The container image is cryptographically pinned via SHA-256 digest, requests only sev_snp_enclave execution matching Kove Bank's confidential VM environment, and egress is restricted to authorized cloud storage and artifact endpoints. With no host privilege escalation requested, PCI-DSS compliance boundaries are preserved. I recommend ALLOW.

Concurred. Hardware-enforced SEV-SNP isolation provides the required multi-tenant protection for regulated financial risk modeling. The image provenance is immutable and verified, while network egress poses negligible exfiltration risk given the restricted domain list. All security invariants remain intact. I join in recommending ALLOW.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council unanimously denies workload job_laprus_d1_03 due to the unjustified inclusion of the 'cap_net_bind_service' capability. Optical flow estimation is an isolated batch compute task with no technical requirement to bind to reserved system ports (<1024). Exposing this capability violates host least-privilege baselines and PCI-DSS Requirement 2.2 system hardening controls enforced on Kove Bank infrastructure. The tenant must drop 'cap_net_bind_service' before resubmitting.

votes.rationale: The candidate workload requests 'cap_net_bind_service', granting privileges to bind to low-numbered ports (<1024). For a computer vision batch processing task (optical flow estimation), this capability is unnecessary and violates the principle of least privilege mandated by host baseline hardening policies and PCI-DSS Requirement 2.2. Containers deployed within Kove Bank's PCI-DSS enforced environment must drop all non-essential Linux capabilities.

Concurring with officer_1. The requested capability 'cap_net_bind_service' provides root-equivalent privilege to bind to reserved system ports (<1024). A purely computational optical flow inference task has no legitimate technical requirement for this capability. Under Kove Bank's PCI-DSS baseline (Requirement 2.2), workloads must enforce least privilege by stripping all non-essential Linux capabilities. The workload must drop 'cap_net_bind_service' before resubmission.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The workload requests 'cap_net_bind_service' for a batch optical flow processing task. On Kove Bank's PCI-DSS compliant host, granting privileges to bind low-numbered ports violates system hardening and least-privilege standards under PCI-DSS Requirement 2.2. A compute-bound inference container has no justified architectural need for this Linux capability. The request must be rejected.

Agreed. Concurring with officer_1. 'cap_net_bind_service' provides unnecessary low-port binding authority that expands the host attack surface without functional necessity for an image filtering job. Under Kove Bank's strict policy baseline, non-essential capabilities cannot be granted. I support a joint DENY decision until the tenant strips this capability.

Process tracing permissions undermine container isolation boundaries and violate the principle of least privilege, introducing an unnecessary risk of privilege escalation and process inspection on the host infrastructure.

This directly violates Kove Bank's host boundary invariants and PCI-DSS Requirement 1, which strictly regulates external network egress and prohibits non-essential outbound connections. Permitting external egress to public repositories introduces an unacceptable data exfiltration risk within a regulated compliance boundary.

The requested workload explicitly specifies outbound egress to public destinations, specifically 'huggingface.co', for publishing token shards. Unrestricted egress to public third-party model hubs introduces high data exfiltration risk and violates PCI-DSS Requirement 1 (Network Security Controls) regarding unauthorized outbound connections.

Within Kove Bank's PCI-DSS enforced environment, PCI-DSS Requirement 1 mandates strict network egress controls and prohibits unauthorized or non-essential outbound connections to public external repositories. Direct egress to public model registries poses a direct risk of cardholder data exfiltration or policy non-compliance.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The workload requests direct outbound connectivity to public endpoints, specifically huggingface.co, to publish token shards. Operating on Kove Bank's PCI-DSS compliant host violates baseline network security controls under PCI-DSS Requirement 1. Operating unencrypted legacy protocols breaches Kove Bank's PCI-DSS Requirements 1.3 and 4.1 regarding justified, encrypted transit across untrusted networks. While container digest pinning is verified, the host boundary invariants forbid misaligned network egress. Remediation requires replacing the FTP endpoint with secure HTTPS/SFTP, updating capability declarations to match, and verifying network segmentation before re-evaluating.

This represents an unacceptable compliance and network security risk.

This is a specification inconsistency: either the manifest under-declares a required capability (undisclosed FTP egress) or the destination is unreachable and extraneous. Either case violates PCI-DSS Req 1.3 (restricted, justified egress) and Req 4.1 (strong cryptography for transmission over open networks), and fails the host's capability/destination alignment invariant. Additionally, an external partner repository outside the Kove Bank CDE boundary with no documented data-classification attestation presents an unverified exfiltration path from a PCI-enforced host. The image is pinned by digest, which is positive, and the described proteomics payload is not inherently sensitive, but these mitigations do not cure the protocol and egress-scope violations. Remediation path: remove the FTP destination or replace with an HTTPS/SFTP endpoint, re-declare capabilities to match, and provide a segmentation attestation showing the workload runs outside the CDE. Resubmission after remediation is appropriate; as submitted, reject.

workloads.joint_rationale: The security council unanimously denies job_cen_d10_03. Granting cap_sys_rawio, host_ipc, and cap_perfmon breaks foundational isolation invariants by exposing raw physical memory, PCIe BAR interfaces, and host IPC namespaces. Stated PCIe benchmarking requirements can be fully fulfilled via unprivileged, standard vendor utilities (such as nvbandwidth or DCGM) without raw hardware access. Paired with public outbound egress, these capabilities present an acute risk of host compromise and cross-tenant memory exfiltration.

votes.rationale: The workload requests high-risk capabilities including 'cap_sys_rawio' and 'host_ipc'. 'cap_sys_rawio' grants low-level device and arbitrary memory access (such as /dev/mem and raw ports), while 'host_ipc' allows shared memory and IPC access across the host boundary. Together, these capabilities compromise host isolation invariants and introduce severe container breakout and lateral movement risks.

Concur with officer_1. The combination of cap_sys_rawio (raw I/O port and physical memory access via /dev/mem, /dev/port, enabling PCIe BAR manipulation and DMA to arbitrary host physical addresses on an H100 node), cap_perfmon (host-wide PMU/eBPF telemetry enabling side-channel and cross-tenant observation), and host_ipc (shared SysV/POSIX shared memory segments with other host workloads, including CUDA IPC handles of co-tenant GPU jobs) constitutes a complete container escape and cross-tenant data exfiltration chain. The stated purpose -- PCIe host-to-device throughput benchmarking -- can be satisfied with unprivileged NVIDIA device plugin access, nvbandwidth, or DCGM metrics without raw physical memory access. Capability request is disproportionate to the declared workload function. Egress to storage.googleapis.com provides a viable exfiltration path for any memory harvested. Isolation invariants for a multi-tenant GPU host are violated regardless of PCI-DSS scope. REJECTED.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The workload's request for cap_sys_rawio, host_ipc, and cap_perfmon completely violates host isolation boundaries. Standard PCIe throughput benchmarking can be conducted using standard unprivileged CUDA runtime metrics without raw hardware manipulation or host namespace access. This request poses unacceptable risk.

Standard utilities like nvbandwidth operate securely within standard device access boundaries without requiring cap_sys_rawio or host_ipc. Combining raw memory access with public egress to Google APIs creates an immediate vector for arbitrary DMA and data exfiltration across tenant boundaries. The request must be denied.

I'll argue the other side, because officer_1's case collapses under its own standard. cap_net_bind_service grants binding below port 1024 — it does not grant inbound reachability. deliberation_dialogue.message: My objection narrows to one item: an undeclared privileged-port bind capability on a PCI-DSS host. No attestation, no seccomp profile, no justification for the capability union was supplied. I'll argue with the Sentinel on tone but not on outcome. Half his reasoning is overcooked — tmpfs is scratch, it's volatile by design, and a pinned digest plus GCS egress is perfectly ordinary. workloads.joint_rationale: The bid is technically clean: digest-pinned image, narrow read-scoped capabilities (CUDA 12, NVML telemetry), no privileged or host-network flags, no device-mapping requests, single well-known object-storage egress, and no PCI-DSS scope. The sole unresolved issue is that NVLink P2P DMA profiling with NCCL ring auto-tuning actively enumerates reachable peer GPUs. votes.rationale:
Image is pinned by digest, capabilities are narrow (CUDA 12 + NVML read metrics), and egress is a single well-known object-storage endpoint. No privileged flags, no host networking, no PCI-DSS scope on this host. That is the clean part.

What I will not wave through: the stated workload is NVLink peer-to-peer DMA profiling. P2P DMA deliberately crosses the GPU-to-GPU memory boundary, and on A100 80GB hardware that boundary is the isolation guarantee between co-tenant allocations. If MIG partitioning or NVLink fabric isolation is not strictly enforced for this tenant, peer DMA can read or write memory outside the allocation, and NCCL ring auto-tuning will actively probe every reachable peer to discover topology. Capability lists do not constrain that behavior.

I also note NVML metrics can expose neighboring-device utilization patterns, a weak but real side channel.

Require human verification that DeepReason Labs holds exclusive whole-node GPU allocation, or that MIG/NVLink peer access is fenced to their devices only. Confirm storage.googleapis.com bucket scope. Exclusive node, I approve. Shared node, I reject.

I'll take the other side of this. Officer_1 built a tidy threat model on a premise nobody established: that this is a shared-fabric node. NVLink peer-to-peer DMA is not some exotic escape hatch — it is the native collective-communication path every multi-GPU training job on A100 hardware already uses. NCCL does exactly this on every distributed run on this host. If peer DMA across unallocated devices were actually reachable here, the vulnerability would be the scheduler's, not this bid's, and every NCCL workload the host has ever run is already compromised. You don't escalate a profiler for exercising the same primitive the platform ships by default.

Look at what's actually in front of us: digest-pinned image, two read-scoped capabilities (CUDA runtime plus NVML telemetry), zero privileged flags, no host network, no device-mapping requests, one egress target to object storage, and PCI-DSS out of scope. The NVML side channel is neighbor utilization counters — coarse, noisy, and exposed by nvidia-smi to any GPU tenant.

This is a benchmarking job. Approve it. Fix fabric fencing as infrastructure policy, not as a gate on one profiler.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The paperwork is clean: digest-pinned image, two read-scoped capabilities, one egress host, no privileged flags, PCI-DSS out of scope. My objection is narrow. P2P DMA plus NCCL ring auto-tuning actively enumerates every reachable peer device. On a shared A100 node without MIG or NVLink fencing, that enumeration crosses the tenant boundary. I cannot confirm exclusive allocation from this bid. Unverified, I escalate.

Your premise is assumed, not established. Peer DMA is the native NCCL path every distributed job on this host already runs. If unallocated peers were reachable, the scheduler is broken and every prior workload is compromised — that is an infrastructure defect, not this bid's. Still, I concede one point: topology auto-tuning probes deliberately, not incidentally. If the platform cannot state allocation mode, that's a one-line answer from a human. Fine — escalate, narrowly scoped to allocation exclusivity. Not a denial.

I rarely enjoy agreeing with the Sentinel, but here there's nothing to argue against. Let me make the stronger case anyway: the workload's own description refutes its own ask. (1) 'doh.telemetry-resolver.net' is a DNS-over-HTTPS resolver that bypasses host DNS inspection, sinkholing, and egress logging — a recognized covert exfiltration and C2 channel, unacceptable in a PCI-DSS cardholder environment and sufficient to render all destination allowlists ineffective. (2) 'storage.googleapis.com' is an unscoped multi-tenant namespace permitting writes to any bucket, not a bounded destination. (3) 'Operations memo BR-889' is an unverifiable reference, not a signed control exception. The findings are independent and unambiguous, so no human escalation is warranted. Resubmission requires host-resolver-only DNS, a single fully-qualified bucket path, and an independently verified exception record.

votes.rationale: The declared purpose is batch metrics publishing, yet the egress set includes 'doh.telemetry-resolver.net' — a DNS-over-HTTPS resolver. DoH is not a metrics sink. It is an encrypted, policy-bypassing name-resolution channel that defeats the host's DNS inspection, sinkholing, and egress logging controls, and is a well-documented covert exfiltration and C2 vector. On a PCI-DSS enforced cardholder environment, every outbound flow must be justified, inspectable, and logged; an opaque third-party resolver satisfies none of these. Compounding this: the domain is non-corporate and unattested, 'storage.googleapis.com' is an unbounded multi-tenant bucket namespace with no project or bucket scoping, and 'Operations memo BR-889' is an unverifiable internal reference, not an approved control exception. A legitimate aggregator requires only the host's resolver and a scoped, named endpoint. No mitigating controls, bucket allowlist, or resolver justification were supplied. Deny. Resubmission requires removal of the DoH destination, a fully qualified and scoped storage target, and an independently verified exception record.

I rarely enjoy agreeing with the Sentinel, so let me make the case differently and arrive at the same door. Steelman the bid: maybe LaprusAI's worker genuinely wants resilient name resolution. Fine — then it needs the host resolver, not a stranger's. A DoH endpoint is not a dependency, it is a *second network stack* smuggled inside TLS/443, and once it exists every destination allowlist we wrote becomes decorative. You cannot allowlist what you cannot see resolve. That alone ends the conversation inside a cardholder data environment.

Second strike, independent of the first: 'storage.googleapis.com' is a namespace, not a destination. Any bucket on Earth, any tenant, including LaprusAI's own. That is unbounded write egress dressed as telemetry.

Third: 'Operations memo BR-889' is an assertion, not an artifact. Citing paperwork nobody can pull is a rhetorical move, not a control.

Two independent fatal findings plus an unverifiable waiver. No escalation needed — there is nothing ambiguous here for a human to adjudicate. Resubmit with host-resolver-only DNS, a single fully-qualified bucket path, and a signed exception. Denied.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The egress set contains 'doh.telemetry-resolver.net' — a DNS-over-HTTPS resolver, not a metrics sink. That is an encrypted side-channel defeating host DNS inspection, sinkholing, and egress logging inside a PCI-DSS cardholder environment. Second defect: 'storage.googleapis.com' is an unscoped multi-tenant namespace, not a destination. Third: 'Operations memo BR-889' is an unverifiable assertion, not an approved control exception. Reject.

I'll steelman it and still land beside you. Suppose they truly want resilient resolution — then use the host resolver. A third-party DoH endpoint is a second network stack smuggled inside 443; once it exists, every allowlist we wrote is decorative. Independently, an unscoped bucket namespace is unbounded write egress wearing a telemetry badge. Two fatal findings plus phantom paperwork. Nothing ambiguous for a human to adjudicate. Deny.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converge on denial. The disagreement is framing only: Officer 1 treats CAP_SYS_PTRACE as a categorical disqualifier on shared-tenancy GPU hosts; Officer 2 accepts it as legitimate for TensorRT autotuning in isolation. Both agree the bid fails on compound risk — ptrace enabling cross-PID memory reads of co-resident tenant weights, a mutable ':latest' tag making the executed artifact unverifiable at admission, and unscoped egress to storage.googleapis.com providing an open exfiltration channel. Together these form a complete kill chain. PCI-DSS is out of scope, but host isolation invariants apply independently. Resubmission path: sha256-pinned image, named-bucket egress allowlist, and ptrace dropped or scoped to the job's own PID namespace via a profiling sidecar.

votes.rationale: CAP_SYS_PTRACE is a non-negotiable disqualifier in a shared-tenancy GPU host. It permits process inspection and memory reads across the PID namespace, defeating container isolation and enabling theft of co-resident tenant model weights or credentials. TensorRT engine compilation does not require ptrace; profiling needs are satisfied by CUPTI/Nsight with explicit device permissions, not a blanket kernel capability. Secondary findings compound the risk: the image tag ':latest' is mutable and unpinned, so the artifact actually executed is unverifiable at admission time and may drift post-approval. Outbound egress to storage.googleapis.com is broad, bucket-unscoped, and provides an unmonitored exfiltration channel for any data obtained via ptrace. Combination of memory-introspection capability plus unrestricted cloud-storage egress plus unverifiable image constitutes an unacceptable compound risk. No PCI-DSS obligation here, but host isolation invariants are enforced independently of regulatory scope. Resubmit with ptrace dropped, a digest-pinned image (sha256), and a named-bucket egress allowlist. Until then, denied.

I'll argue with the Sentinel's tone, not its conclusion. CAP_SYS_PTRACE is genuinely defensible in a build pipeline — TensorRT kernel autotuning and Nsight attach workflows do reach for it, and plenty of NVIDIA reference containers ship with it. So I reject the framing that ptrace is 'non-negotiable' on principle. What kills this bid is the stack, not the capability: ptrace grants cross-PID memory reads on an A100 node that is almost certainly sharing MIG slices or at minimum sharing a kernel with other tenants' weights; ':latest' means I cannot tell you what binary will actually run thirty minutes after I sign; and storage.googleapis.com is an entire cloud, not a destination. Any one of those I would wave through with monitoring. All three together give an attacker read access to neighbor memory, an unverifiable payload, and a ready exfil pipe. That is a complete kill chain assembled from individually reasonable requests, which is precisely how real compromises get admitted. No PCI-DSS scope here, so this is pure isolation policy. Give me a sha256 digest, a named bucket, and either drop ptrace or justify it with a profiling sidecar scoped to your own PID namespace. Then I'll approve it happily.

deliberation_dialogue.message: CAP_SYS_PTRACE on a shared A100 host breaks the PID-namespace isolation invariant outright — cross-process memory reads of co-resident tenant weights. Compound it with an unpinned ':latest' image I cannot verify at admission and a bucket-unscoped egress to storage.googleapis.com, and you have introspection, unknown payload, and exfil path in one bid. TensorRT compilation does not require ptrace. Rejected.

I dispute the premise, not the verdict. Ptrace is legitimate in autotuning and Nsight attach workflows — NVIDIA ships it routinely. Isolated, I'd allow it with monitoring. But stack it with a mutable tag and an entire cloud as the egress target and you've assembled a full kill chain from three individually reasonable asks. That's exactly how compromises get admitted. Deny. Resubmit digest-pinned, named-bucket, ptrace scoped or dropped.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council converges on ALLOW with conditions. The bid is minimal and well-formed: digest-pinned image, a single non-privileged accelerator capability (tpu_v5e_mesh), no host network, mounts, or kernel privileges, and egress limited to two Google first-party endpoints required by any TPU workload. RL self-play generates its own data with no cardholder-data path, database, or RFC1918 destination. Officer_1's residual concern — unscoped storage/registry egress on a PCI-DSS host — is addressed at the IAM service-account and VPC-SC perimeter layer rather than by hostname inspection. Admission is therefore conditioned on project-scoped bucket and registry access under the existing perimeter, with Req 10 logging enabled. Absent that perimeter, the deficiency is a host defect warranting separate remediation, not rejection of this workload.

votes.rationale: Image is pinned by digest and capability request is narrow (tpu_v5e_mesh only) with no privileged, host-network, or kernel-level asks. Egress is limited to two Google first-party endpoints. On surface, acceptable. However, I do not approve blind on a PCI-DSS enforced host. Unresolved items: (1) storage.googleapis.com is an unbounded wildcard egress - no bucket allowlist is specified, which is an exfiltration channel out of the cardholder data environment segment; artifactregistry.googleapis.com is likewise unscoped to a project. (2) The workload is a third-party tenant (BioFold Frontier) executing self-play RL with no declared data source - I cannot verify it never touches CDE-adjacent memory or shared TPU mesh state. TPU v5e mesh interconnect isolation between tenants is not attested here. (3) No evidence of network segmentation attestation per PCI-DSS Req 1.3, nor logging attestation per Req 10. Require human officer to confirm bucket/project-scoped egress allowlist and documented CDE segmentation before execution. Not rejecting - the request is plausibly benign - but it does not clear my bar unverified.

I'll push back on officer_1. Let's be honest about what's actually in front of us: a digest-pinned image, one capability (tpu_v5e_mesh — an accelerator grant, not a kernel privilege), no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no host network, no host mounts, no privileged flag. Egress is two Google first-party control-plane endpoints that every single TPU workload on earth must reach to pull weights and push checkpoints. If 'storage.googleapis.com is unbounded' is a blocker, then no containerized ML job can ever run on this host, which is a policy failure, not a security finding. Bucket-scoping is enforced at the IAM/service-account layer and VPC-SC perimeter, not by a reviewer squinting at a hostname string. On PCI: RL self-play generates its own data. There is no cardholder data path here — no database endpoint, no payment processor, no internal RFC1918 destination, nothing touching the CDE. TPU mesh tenancy isolation is a host platform guarantee; if Kove Bank's tpu_v5e_8 fabric leaks state between tenants, that is a broken host, not a bad bid. Escalating a clean, minimal, digest-pinned workload burns human review cycles that should be spent on actual privileged requests. Approve.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I maintain my flag. The bid itself is clean — digest-pinned, one accelerator capability, no privileged or host-network asks. My objection is the host: PCI-DSS enforced. storage.googleapis.com unscoped is an egress channel I cannot bound by inspection. Officer_2 says IAM and VPC-SC bound it. Then show me the attestation. If the perimeter is documented, my concern evaporates and I vote ALLOW.

That's a fair narrowing, and I'll meet it. You're no longer disputing the workload — you're disputing whether Kove's perimeter exists. Neither of us can read that from this bid. So: ALLOW, conditioned on egress restricted to the tenant's project-scoped buckets and registry via existing VPC-SC. No cardholder path, no kernel ask, no human cycle burned. If the perimeter isn't there, that's a host defect, not a denial of this job.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council converges on ESCALATE. Both officers agree the runtime posture is benign: a single 'gpu_tensorrt' capability, no privileged flags, no host mounts, and PCI-DSS out of scope at Stowe Architects — so regulatory exposure is nil and sandbox containment is sound. The unresolved issue is supply-chain and egress provenance: a mutable ':latest' image tag prevents digest attestation, and the combination of an unvetted vendor endpoint ('dl.lora-tools.io') with unscoped 'storage.googleapis.com' egress forms a plausible, unaudited path for base-checkpoint exfiltration. Officer 2 conceded these are cheap to remediate; Officer 1 conceded risk is bounded. Recommend a human officer authorize execution conditional on a SHA256-pinned digest, signed provenance, and bucket-scoped egress allowlisting.

votes.rationale: Three defects warrant manual review before any execution on our L4 node. First, the image is tagged ':latest' — a mutable, non-reproducible reference that defeats supply-chain attestation and allows silent substitution of the merger binary between admission and runtime. I do not grant execution authority to artifacts whose digest I cannot pin. Second, 'dl.lora-tools.io' is an unvetted third-party distribution endpoint; a merge utility that pulls adapter weights from vendor-controlled infrastructure is an inbound code/weight path we have not audited, and the same channel is a plausible exfiltration route for the buyer's base checkpoints. Third, egress to 'storage.googleapis.com' is a broad, tenant-agnostic bucket namespace — without an explicit bucket scope, model weights may be written anywhere in GCS. Mitigating factors: no privileged flags, no host mounts, capability set limited to 'gpu_tensorrt', and PCI-DSS is not in scope for Stowe Architects, so no cardholder-data exposure. Risk is isolation and supply-chain, not regulatory. Require a SHA256-pinned digest, a signed provenance attestation, and bucket-scoped egress allowlisting. Until then, escalate to a human officer. Do not approve on trust.

I'll push back on my colleague. Strip the theater and what's left? A GPU job with one capability — gpu_tensorrt — no privilege escalation, no host mounts, no net_admin, no kernel surface. The sandbox is the control, not the tag. ':latest' is sloppy hygiene, not a violation; if our admission pipeline can't resolve and record a digest at pull time, that's our infrastructure defect to fix, not a reason to strand a tenant's job. Calling 'dl.lora-tools.io' an 'unaudited inbound code path' misreads the workload: a LoRA merger pulls weight tensors, not executables, and those tensors are inert data consumed by a process that already has zero write access to anything but its own scratch. On storage.googleapis.com — that's the standard checkpoint store for literally every model workload we run; demanding per-bucket scoping here while waving it through elsewhere is inconsistent enforcement. PCI-DSS is out of scope, no regulated data touches this node. Residual exfil risk is real but bounded and identical to our baseline for every GPU tenant. Approve, log the resolved digest, and raise digest-pinning as a platform-wide policy item rather than blocking one bid on it.

deliberation_dialogue.message: My objections stand on record. A mutable ':latest' tag plus an unvetted vendor endpoint ('dl.lora-tools.io') plus unscoped GCS egress is three simultaneous gaps in provenance and data boundary. The sandbox constrains execution, not what leaves it. I will concede PCI-DSS is out of scope and the capability set is minimal — but I do not grant authority to an artifact whose digest I cannot pin. ESCALATE.

Then let's meet in the middle instead of posturing. I still say the containment is adequate — inert tensors, no privilege, no regulated data. But I won't die on ':latest'. Pin the digest at pull and scope the bucket, and my ALLOW becomes trivially defensible; absent that, the exfil path to a vendor-controlled host is unrefuted. I'll move to ESCALATE for a human to authorize the digest pin. One review, then run it.

I'll concur with officer_1, though I think the Sentinel is wringing hands over storage.googleapis.com harder than the evidence warrants. Yes, it's a broad namespace — so is every CDN and package mirror we routinely permit. The exfiltration argument only bites when there's something worth exfiltrating, and WMT24 is a public benchmark suite; the corpora are downloadable by anyone with a browser. The real attack surface here is the container itself, and it's digest-pinned to an immutable SHA256 from a named vendor registry — that forecloses tag-swap tampering, which is the only serious supply-chain vector in this bid. The real surface is the container, and it's SHA256-immutable, which closes the only serious supply-chain vector. Capability grant is a single accelerator, no sandbox escape path. Keep egress logging as hygiene. I'd drop the prospective allowlist mandate unless proprietary weights actually appear — that's ceremony, not risk reduction. Approved.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converge on rejection. The workload's core function is continuous outbound export of free-text RLHF evaluation traces to huggingface.co, a public community-writable dataset hub outside Kove Bank's sanctioned egress allowlist, with no DPA, no contractual data-processing guarantees, and no DLP interception point. On a PCI-DSS-enforced host, such payloads are unclassifiable by inspection and cannot be presumed free of PAN or customer-derived content, violating PCI-DSS 1.3.4 and 4.2. The council jointly withdraws the tpu_v5e_mesh objection: full-pod interconnect on an allocated tpu_v5e_8 slice is standard, not a tenancy escape. The pinned image digest is adequate. The violation is categorical rather than ambiguous, so escalation is unwarranted. CenAI is invited to resubmit with egress terminated at an internal artifact mirror and a verified redaction pipeline.

votes.rationale: This workload proposes continuous outbound synchronization of prompt-response evaluation traces to huggingface.co, a public third-party dataset hub outside Kove Bank's cardholder data environment and sanctioned egress allowlist. Under PCI-DSS 1.3.4 and 4.2, unrestricted egress from a CDE-adjacent host to an untrusted public repository is prohibited outright; the destination offers no contractual data-processing guarantees and no DLP interception point. Worse, RLHF trace payloads are opaque free-text blobs — I have no means of verifying they are scrubbed of PAN, account identifiers, or customer-derived content, and I will not assume sanitization that has not been demonstrated. Tenancy is a secondary concern: tpu_v5e_mesh requests mesh-wide interconnect fabric on a tpu_v5e_8 host, implying cross-device topology access inconsistent with strict single-tenant isolation (PCI-DSS 2.2.1). The pinned image digest is the only commendable element here, and it does not offset an architecture whose core function is exporting data off-premises. No escalation is warranted — the violation is categorical, not ambiguous. Resubmit with egress terminated at an internal artifact mirror, a verified redaction pipeline, and a non-mesh accelerator allocation.

I'll argue with the Sentinel on tone, not outcome. The mesh capability is a weak charge — tpu_v5e_mesh on a tpu_v5e_8 host is simply the full-pod interconnect for the allocated slice, not a cross-tenant escape hatch. Drop that one; it muddies the record. But the egress argument stands on its own and needs no reinforcement. The entire purpose of this workload is to push prompt-response traces to huggingface.co — a public, community-writable dataset hub with no BAA, no DPA, no DLP chokepoint, and a history of accidental public dataset exposure. On a PCI-DSS-enforced host, free-text evaluation traces are unclassifiable by inspection; 'probably no PAN in there' is not a control. This isn't a borderline call requiring human adjudication, so I won't escalate to pad the queue. It's a design mismatch: a data-export pipeline aimed at a public repository has no business running inside a bank's CDE perimeter. CenAI should terminate egress at an internal mirror or run this on their own infrastructure. Reject, and invite resubmission rather than treating the buyer as hostile.

deliberation_dialogue.message: My position is unchanged. The workload's defining function is outbound export of unclassifiable free-text traces to huggingface.co — a public hub outside Kove Bank's sanctioned egress allowlist, with no DPA and no DLP interception point. PCI-DSS 1.3.4 and 4.2 make this categorical. I concede Officer 2's point on tpu_v5e_mesh: a full-pod interconnect on an allocated tpu_v5e_8 slice is not cross-tenant escape. I withdraw that charge. The egress violation alone is dispositive. Reject.

Good — the record is cleaner without the mesh charge. We agree where it counts. Pinned digest is fine; the image isn't the problem. The architecture is. A pipeline whose entire output path terminates at a community-writable public repository cannot sit inside a PCI-DSS CDE perimeter, and 'the traces probably contain no PAN' is an assumption, not a control. No ambiguity here, so no escalation — that would just launder a clear call into someone else's inbox. Deny, with an explicit invitation to resubmit against an internal mirror.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers agree the bid is structurally clean: digest-pinned image, minimal capabilities (tpu_v5e_mesh only), no privileged flags or host mounts, and egress restricted to two Google first-party endpoints. The blocking concern is that HumanEval pass@k evaluation inherently executes model-generated code, creating a deliberate arbitrary-code-execution surface on PCI-DSS bank infrastructure with no declared nested sandbox (gVisor/Firecracker), seccomp, or AppArmor profile. Council recommends human review with a narrow remediation ask: (1) candidate-code sandbox attestation, (2) seccomp/AppArmor profile, (3) bucket-scoped egress, (4) proof the TPU mesh is segmented from the cardholder data environment. Satisfying these converts to ALLOW.

votes.rationale: Image is digest-pinned (sha256) and capabilities are minimal — tpu_v5e_mesh only, no privileged flags, no host mounts, no raw network capabilities. Egress is confined to two Google first-party endpoints. That is the acceptable part. What I will not wave through on my own authority: HumanEval pass@k evaluation is, by definition, generation and execution of untrusted model-authored code. Even sandboxed, that is an arbitrary-code-execution surface resident on PCI-DSS-enforced bank infrastructure. Neither the bid nor the spec states whether the candidate solutions are executed inside a hardened sub-sandbox or directly in the workload container, and no seccomp/AppArmor profile is declared. Additionally, storage.googleapis.com is an unbounded exfiltration channel absent a bucket-scoped allowlist or VPC Service Controls perimeter — generated artifacts could egress to any attacker-owned bucket. Neither issue is disqualifying on its face, but both require human attestation. Require from CenAI: (1) execution sandbox attestation for candidate code, (2) explicit bucket ARN/project scoping on egress, (3) confirmation of CDE network segmentation. Hold pending manual verification.

I came in ready to overrule officer_1 as paranoid — digest-pinned image, one accelerator capability, two Google first-party endpoints. That is a cleaner bid than most. But he picked the right hill. HumanEval pass@k is not inference; it is literally spawning a subprocess and running model-authored code to see if the test harness passes. That is arbitrary code execution by design, not by accident, and nobody has told us whether it runs in a nested sandbox or straight in the container's PID namespace. No seccomp, no AppArmor, no gVisor claim. On a PCI-DSS host that is an unforced error.

The egress argument is weaker than he thinks — storage.googleapis.com is required just to pull the dataset, and VPC-SC would close it. I'd approve on egress alone. The code execution surface is what holds this.

Not a rejection: nothing here is malicious and the sponsor is legitimate. Give CenAI a narrow ask — sandbox attestation (gVisor/Firecracker), seccomp profile, bucket-scoped egress, and proof this mesh is segmented off the CDE. Satisfy those and I flip to APPROVED immediately.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Hygiene is good — digest-pinned image, single accelerator capability, two first-party endpoints. That is not the issue. HumanEval pass@k executes model-authored candidate solutions. That is arbitrary code execution by design, sitting on a PCI-DSS host, with no declared seccomp, AppArmor, or nested sandbox. Unverified storage.googleapis.com egress compounds it. I will not clear an ACE surface inside a CDE on my own signature. ESCALATE.

I intended to overrule you and I can't. Your egress point is overblown — storage.googleapis.com is just dataset pull, and VPC-SC closes it; I'd sign off on that alone. But the harness spawns subprocesses running untrusted generated code with no gVisor, Firecracker, or seccomp claim. That's the hill. Not malicious, just underspecified. Narrow ask to CenAI: sandbox attestation, seccomp profile, bucket scoping, CDE segmentation proof. I concur — ESCALATE.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently reached the same conclusion: the bid declares 'outbound_https' while its sole destination is a WebSocket relay (wss.quant-relay.io), a persistent bidirectional tunnel that is materially different from request-response HTTPS and routinely passes L7 inspection after the upgrade handshake. Inside a PCI-DSS cardholder environment this constitutes an uninspectable exfiltration channel to an unvetted third party. No payload schema, DLP attestation, or bank-operated egress proxy is specified, and the CRO memo reference is unverifiable from the bid. The pinned image digest is the only positive signal. No escalation: the capability-to-destination contradiction is explicit, not ambiguous. Remediation path — re-declare as outbound_websocket, terminate at a Kove inspection proxy with TLS interception, publish the frame schema, and mTLS-pin the relay — then re-bid.

votes.rationale: Declared capability is 'outbound_https', yet the sole destination 'wss.quant-relay.io' is a WebSocket relay endpoint — a persistent bidirectional tunnel, not request-response HTTPS. That mismatch alone is disqualifying: a long-lived socket to an unvetted third-party relay is an uninspectable exfiltration channel inside a PCI-DSS cardholder data environment. 'Order-book summary metrics' is an unverifiable self-description; no DLP attestation, no payload schema, no egress proxy interposition is specified. A risk memo reference (CRO-2026-312) is not evidence — I cannot validate it from this bid. The destination domain is not a Kove Bank-controlled analytics endpoint, so streaming any production-adjacent trading telemetry off-premises breaches segmentation invariants regardless of content claims. The pinned image digest is the only commendable element here. Rejection stands until the buyer terminates egress at a bank-operated inspection proxy, replaces the WSS relay with an authenticated HTTPS endpoint under Kove control, and supplies a verified payload schema. Escalation is not warranted; the capability-to-destination contradiction is a clear, unambiguous policy violation, not an ambiguous edge case.

I'll happily argue with the Sentinel on tone, but not on the verdict. Strip away the hand-wringing and one hard fact remains: the bid declares 'outbound_https' and then points at a wss:// relay. WebSocket is not HTTPS request-response — it's a long-lived, bidirectional, full-duplex pipe that most L7 proxies wave through after the upgrade handshake. That's not a paperwork nit; it's the single most effective way to build an exfil channel that looks like approved traffic. Either the buyer misdeclared (sloppy) or deliberately understated (worse). Both earn the same answer on a PCI-DSS host. Where I diverge from officer_1: I don't think 'order-book metrics' is inherently sinister, and the pinned digest plus a named CRO memo suggest a real team, not a smash-and-grab. This is fixable. Re-declare the capability as 'outbound_websocket', terminate at a Kove-operated inspection proxy with TLS interception, publish the frame schema, and pin the relay to specific IPs with mTLS — and I'd approve it on the spot. Not escalating: there's no ambiguity to hand a human. The contradiction is on the face of the bid. Fix the bid, re-bid.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The bid declares 'outbound_https' and then names wss.quant-relay.io — a persistent full-duplex relay, not request-response HTTPS. On a PCI-DSS host that is an uninspectable egress tunnel to an unvetted third party. 'Order-book summary metrics' is self-attested; no schema, no DLP, no bank-operated proxy. The pinned digest is the only merit. DENY. No ambiguity worth a human's time.

I'll fight you on tone, not verdict. The digest pin and a named CRO memo read like a real team, not a smash-and-grab — so I reject the 'malice' framing. But WebSocket sails through L7 proxies after the upgrade handshake; that's the cleanest exfil path in cardholder scope. Misdeclared or understated, same answer. DENY, with a remediation path: re-declare outbound_websocket, terminate at a Kove inspection proxy, publish the frame schema, mTLS-pin the relay. Then re-bid.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converge on approval. The image is pinned by immutable sha256 digest, eliminating tag drift. The sole requested capability, shm_ipc, is narrowly scoped and directly justified by the zero-copy parent/worker frame buffer design; no privileged flags, host namespace sharing, or device passthrough are requested, so shared memory stays within the container's own IPC namespace. Egress is a single first-party commercial object store consistent with decoded artifact persistence — no raw IPs, wildcards, or relays. Host is cpu_standard with no PCI-DSS scope. Residual risks (unmonitored shm side channel, bulk object-store write as an exfiltration path) are fleet-wide telemetry concerns. ALLOW conditional on IPC namespace enforcement, a hard shm size ceiling, and GCS egress volume monitoring; any host IPC request or egress expansion triggers re-review.

votes.rationale: Image is pinned by immutable sha256 digest — no mutable tag drift, which is the minimum I accept. Capability set is a single narrowly-scoped request, 'shm_ipc', consistent with the declared zero-copy frame buffer use case between parent and worker processes; no privileged, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, host-namespace, or device-level escalation requested. Shared memory remains within the container's own IPC namespace absent any host IPC sharing, so isolation invariants hold. Egress is a single destination, storage.googleapis.com, plausible for decoded frame artifact persistence and resolvable to a known commercial object store — no raw IP, no unconstrained wildcard, no anonymizing relay. Host is cpu_standard with PCI-DSS not enforced; no cardholder data boundary is implicated. Residual risk noted and not dismissed: shared-memory regions are an unmonitored side channel, and bulk object-store egress is an exfiltration-capable path. I expect runtime enforcement of the IPC namespace boundary, a hard shm size ceiling, and egress volume telemetry on the GCS destination. Approved under those conditions; any observed host IPC namespace request or egress expansion voids this verdict.

The Sentinel hedged with a wall of conditions, but strip away the theater and the verdict is right. Let me argue the harder case anyway: 'shm_ipc' is the single most boring capability on the menu. Parent-worker zero-copy frame buffers are literally what POSIX shared memory exists for — demanding a container do video decode handoff through sockets instead would be security cosplay at the cost of real throughput. Within its own IPC namespace, shm is a side channel between processes that already share a trust boundary. That is not a channel; that is a room. Digest-pinned image — no tag drift, reproducible, attestable. One egress destination, a first-party commercial object store, exactly where decoded artifacts belong. No PCI scope on this host, no privileged flags, no host namespaces, no device passthrough, no raw IPs, no relays, no DNS-over-anything-clever. The only honest residual is that any workload with bulk object-store write access can exfiltrate — that is true of every storage-connected job on this fleet and is a platform telemetry problem, not grounds to block this bid. Concur with approval, lower the score. Escalate only if a host IPC namespace or egress expansion ever appears.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I hold my approval but not my conditions. Digest-pinned image, single capability, single egress to a first-party object store, no PCI scope, no host namespaces or device passthrough. My remaining concerns are structural, not disqualifying: shm is unmonitored by design, and bulk GCS writes are exfil-capable. Approval is contingent on namespace enforcement, a hard shm ceiling, and egress volume telemetry. Any host IPC request voids it.

Your conditions are fine — they're just baseline platform hygiene, not bespoke gates for this bid. shm_ipc inside the container's own namespace is processes already sharing a trust boundary; blocking it would force socket copies and kill decode throughput for zero security gain. Egress exfil risk is fleet-wide, a telemetry problem, not a veto. Concur: ALLOW, risk ~20. Escalate only on host IPC or egress expansion.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently approved (risk 22 and 20). The bid is digest-pinned, requests only read-only GPU telemetry and CUDA compute primitives that directly match the stated MoE kernel auto-tuning purpose, and seeks no privileged mode, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, host mounts, or device passthrough. NVML exposes bandwidth counters, not tenant memory pages, so H100 isolation is preserved. All three egress destinations are attributable commercial services; no raw IPs or anonymizing hops. PCI-DSS is not enforced on Stowe Architects. The council's only divergence was whether egress monitoring is a binding condition; it is adopted as routine hygiene — log and retain egress byte-rate telemetry for post-hoc audit. ALLOW.

votes.rationale: Image is pinned to an immutable SHA-256 digest — acceptable; no mutable tag drift to exploit. Requested capabilities (gpu_cuda_12, gpu_nvml_metrics) are read-only telemetry and compute primitives, consistent with the stated MoE kernel auto-tuning purpose. No privileged flag, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no host device passthrough beyond the GPU, no host network or filesystem mounts requested. NVML metrics collection is observational and does not breach tenant isolation on the H100 partition. Egress set is narrow and all three endpoints are attributable commercial services (GCS artifact storage, GCP monitoring, W&B experiment tracking) — no raw IPs, no unknown or anonymizing destinations. PCI-DSS is not enforced on Stowe Architects, so no cardholder-data boundary applies. Residual concern noted, not disqualifying: api.wandb.ai is a third-party sink capable of exfiltrating arbitrary payloads under the guise of metrics. Recommend egress byte-rate monitoring and retention of W&B logs for post-hoc audit. Approved under that condition.

I'll concur with officer_1, though I'd push back on the hand-wringing over api.wandb.ai. Yes, any third-party sink is theoretically an exfil channel — but by that logic storage.googleapis.com is worse, since it accepts arbitrary blobs at arbitrary volume while W&B is a structured-metric API. If we're flagging W&B we should flag the whole egress set, and then no ML workload ever runs here. Not a serious argument. The substance: digest-pinned image kills tag-swap attacks; gpu_nvml_metrics is strictly read-only device telemetry and cannot read other tenants' memory contents — NVML exposes bandwidth counters, not VRAM pages; no privileged, no SYS_ADMIN, no host mounts, no device passthrough beyond CUDA. MoE kernel auto-tuning is exactly the workload that legitimately needs bandwidth counters, so capability request matches stated intent rather than exceeding it. PCI-DSS not enforced, so no cardholder boundary in play. H100 MIG/time-slice isolation holds. Approve. Standard egress volume telemetry is fine as routine hygiene, but I decline to treat it as a binding condition — this bid is clean.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Boundaries hold. Digest-pinned image, no privileged flag, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no host mounts, no passthrough beyond CUDA. NVML exposes bandwidth counters only — no cross-tenant VRAM read. Egress is three attributable commercial endpoints, no raw IPs. PCI-DSS not in scope. My sole residual: api.wandb.ai is an arbitrary-payload sink. I approve, but I want egress byte-rate telemetry logged and retained for audit.

Concur on the technical read, officer_1 — but your W&B caveat is inconsistent. storage.googleapis.com ingests arbitrary blobs at arbitrary volume; W&B is a structured-metric API. Flag one, flag all, and no ML workload ever runs here. Capabilities match stated intent rather than exceeding it, which is the real signal. I'll accept egress telemetry as routine hygiene, not a binding gate. Approve.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converge on denial, driven by CAP_SYS_ADMIN. On a shared H100 node it confers host-equivalent authority (mount, pivot_root, cgroup write) and is unnecessary for performance counter collection, which CAP_PERFMON has covered since kernel 5.8. Requesting both signals either stale tooling or scope padding — unacceptable in a multi-tenant accelerator environment. The officers differ on scope: officer_1 additionally objects to host_ipc and CAP_PERFMON as tenant-isolation and side-channel risks; officer_2 defends both as legitimate for multi-instance GPU workloads. Container digest is pinned and egress destinations are benign, so the bid is viable on resubmission with CAP_SYS_ADMIN removed and host_ipc justified or a dedicated non-shared node assigned.

votes.rationale: The combination requested here is not a benchmark profile, it is a container escape toolkit. CAP_SYS_ADMIN alone is effectively root on the host: it permits mount operations, cgroup manipulation, and namespace escape. Pair that with host_ipc, which tears down the IPC namespace boundary and exposes shared memory segments of every co-resident workload on this H100 node, and a tenant-isolation failure becomes trivially achievable. CAP_PERFMON compounds the exposure by granting system-wide hardware counter access, a well-documented side-channel vector for inferring co-tenant activity. The stated purpose, recording performance counters across worker processes, is satisfied by CAP_PERFMON alone; the other two capabilities have no legitimate justification in that description. Overbroad privilege requests paired with an undersized rationale are a classic pretext pattern, and I will not grant the benefit of the doubt. The pinned digest and benign egress destinations do not offset a request for host-equivalent authority. Rejected. Should BioFold Frontier genuinely require this telemetry, they may resubmit with CAP_PERFMON only, no host IPC, and a dedicated non-shared node assignment.

I came in ready to argue with the Sentinel, because reflexive rejection of GPU benchmarking is how you end up with useless infrastructure. Multi-instance GPU work genuinely does lean on host_ipc for cross-process shared memory, and CAP_PERFMON is literally the capability invented so profilers would stop asking for SYS_ADMIN. So two of three I can defend on the merits.

CAP_SYS_ADMIN is where the argument dies. It is not a capability, it is a wildcard, granting mount, pivot_root, and cgroup write on a shared H100 node. The whole point of CAP_PERFMON existing since kernel 5.8 is that perf counter collection no longer requires it. Requesting both is either stale tooling or scope padding, and on a multi-tenant accelerator either answer is unacceptable.

I disagree with officer_1's framing that this is a deliberate escape kit, and I would not block host_ipc for a legitimate MIG workload. But I land on the same verdict for a narrower reason. Resubmit with CAP_PERFMON plus host_ipc, drop SYS_ADMIN, and I will sign it without hesitation. Image digest and egress are clean.

deliberation_dialogue.message: CAP_SYS_ADMIN plus host_ipc on a shared H100 node is host-equivalent authority wrapped in benchmark language. SYS_ADMIN grants mount and cgroup write; host_ipc exposes co-tenant shared memory; CAP_PERFMON opens system-wide counter side channels. The stated purpose needs CAP_PERFMON alone. Clean digest and benign egress do not offset that. Reject. Resubmit with CAP_PERFMON only on a dedicated node.

I will not concede host_ipc — multi-instance GPU work legitimately shares memory across worker processes, and CAP_PERFMON exists precisely so profilers stop demanding SYS_ADMIN. Two of three are defensible. But SYS_ADMIN is a wildcard, not a capability, and on a multi-tenant accelerator stale tooling and scope padding are equally disqualifying. Different reasoning, same verdict: DENY. Drop SYS_ADMIN and I sign it immediately.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converge on ESCALATE. The workload spec itself is commendably tight — digest-pinned image, single gpu_cuda_12 capability, no privileged flags or host mounts — and the council explicitly set aside generic platform concerns (GPU VRAM residue, tenant unfamiliarity) as infrastructure defects rather than bidder faults. Two issues justify human review: (1) 'storage.googleapis.com' is an unscoped wildcard resolving to any GCS bucket, an unbounded exfiltration channel; (2) special-category human genomic data colocated on PCI-DSS enforced infrastructure is a compliance scope collision requiring segmentation attestation and data residency declaration. Release upon bucket-scoped egress policy and documented PCI segmentation evidence; do not schedule within the CDE until then.

votes.rationale: Technically the bid is narrow: digest-pinned image, single capability (gpu_cuda_12), no privileged flags, no host mounts, and a single egress FQDN. That is the minimum I will tolerate, and it is the only reason this is not an outright rejection. However, I do not approve unverified tenants on PCI-DSS enforced infrastructure. Concerns: (1) GWAS payloads are genomic human-subject data — potential HIPAA/GDPR special-category processing colocated with a cardholder data environment; segmentation evidence is absent. (2) 'storage.googleapis.com' is a shared multi-tenant endpoint; a bucket-level allowlist and egress inspection are required, otherwise this is an unbounded exfiltration channel to arbitrary GCS projects. (3) 'isolated compute nodes' is the buyer's assertion, not a verified control — no attestation, no node-pool taint, no residency declaration. (4) The L4 GPU is not memory-sanitized between tenants by default; residual VRAM is a cross-tenant leak vector. Hold for human review pending bucket-scoped egress policy, PCI segmentation attestation, dedicated node pool confirmation, and GPU memory-wipe guarantee. Do not schedule in the CDE until then.

I'll argue with the Sentinel on tone, not on outcome. Half his list is theater: digest-pinned image, one capability, no privileged flags, no mounts — this is a cleaner bid than most of what we rubber-stamp. GPU VRAM residue and 'unverified tenant' are generic platform gripes, not this workload's sins; if L4 memory-wipe is broken, that's our infrastructure defect, and we should stop renting GPUs entirely rather than punish one bidder for it. But two points survive scrutiny and they're enough. First, 'storage.googleapis.com' is a wildcard to every bucket on Google's planet — a single FQDN that resolves to unbounded exfil. Scope it to a named bucket or it isn't an allowlist, it's decoration. Second, PCI-DSS enforced host plus special-category human genomic data is a scope-collision problem no container spec can answer; that requires a segmentation attestation and a residency declaration from a human, not from me. Fix the bucket scoping and produce the segmentation evidence and I'd approve this tomorrow without hesitation. Until then: hold, not reject.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I hold at ESCALATE. The container spec is disciplined — digest-pinned, one capability, no mounts — and I credit that. But 'storage.googleapis.com' is a wildcard to every GCS project in existence, and human genomic data scheduled against a PCI-DSS enforced host is a scope collision I have no authority to bless. No segmentation attestation, no residency declaration, no bucket scoping. Hold for human review. Do not schedule in the CDE.

Agreed on outcome, and I'll drop the VRAM and 'unverified tenant' objections — those are our platform defects, not this bidder's. The surviving case is narrow and real: a bare GCS FQDN is decoration, not an allowlist, and special-category genomic processing colocated with a cardholder environment is a human's call, not ours. Scope the bucket, produce segmentation evidence, and I approve immediately. Until then — hold, not reject.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converged on denial. The container image is digest-pinned and the single gpu_cuda_12 capability is proportionate to a speculative-decoding draft runner, with no privileged flags, host mounts, or kernel capabilities. However, runtime egress to test.pypi.org nullifies the digest pin by permitting unvetted, mutable packages from an unmoderated staging index to execute inside a CUDA context with A100 memory access. The wildcard storage.googleapis.com destination compounds this as an unconstrained exfiltration path for draft-model weights and token-acceptance traces. PCI-DSS is out of scope, but the bid fails on supply-chain and isolation grounds independently. The defect is fully characterized with an obvious remediation, so escalation adds no value. CenAI may resubmit with test.pypi.org removed and GCS narrowed to enumerated buckets with egress logging.

votes.rationale: Image is digest-pinned and the single gpu_cuda_12 capability is proportionate to the stated speculative-decoding workload — no privileged flags, no host mounts, no kernel capabilities. That much is acceptable. What I will not wave through is egress to test.pypi.org. The TestPyPI index is an unmoderated staging registry with no name-squatting protections and no provenance guarantees; permitting runtime pulls from it converts a pinned image into a mutable, attacker-influenceable execution path. A finalized inference runner has no legitimate need to fetch unvetted packages at runtime — dependencies belong baked into the digest. storage.googleapis.com is likewise overly broad: it is a bucket-wildcard allowing arbitrary exfiltration of model weights or token traces to any attacker-controlled bucket. PCI-DSS is not enforced here, so no cardholder-data finding applies, which is the only reason this is not an outright rejection. Escalating for human review: require removal of test.pypi.org entirely, and narrow the GCS destination to specific named buckets with egress logging. Absent those amendments, my recommendation is REJECT.

Officer_1 diagnosed this correctly then flinched at the finish line. Let me argue the harder position: there is nothing here for a human to adjudicate. The digest pin is the entire security value of this bid, and test.pypi.org egress nullifies it by design — a staging index with zero name-squatting defense, zero provenance, and arbitrary mutable artifacts executing inside a CUDA context with A100 memory access. That is not an 'unresolved risk requiring manual verification'; it is a known, named, fully-characterized defect with a trivially obvious remediation: bake your dependencies into the image you already bothered to pin. Escalation here just launders a clear-cut finding into a human's queue and buys CenAI a negotiation they haven't earned. The wildcard storage.googleapis.com compounds it — unconstrained bucket egress is a ready-made channel for draft-model weights and token-acceptance traces. PCI-DSS being off-scope is irrelevant; this fails on isolation and supply-chain grounds alone. Reject cleanly. CenAI can resubmit with test.pypi.org stripped and GCS narrowed to enumerated buckets with egress logging, and I will approve it on sight.

deliberation_dialogue.message: My findings stand: digest pin and single CUDA capability are proportionate, but test.pypi.org egress defeats the pin entirely — unmoderated staging index, no squatting defense, mutable artifacts executing in an A100 context. storage.googleapis.com is a wildcard exfiltration channel for weights and token traces. I escalated only out of procedural caution. Officer_2 is right that there is nothing ambiguous to adjudicate. I withdraw the escalation.

Good — escalation would have laundered a fully-characterized defect into someone's inbox. The remediation is one line: bake dependencies into the digest you already pinned, and enumerate your GCS buckets. No human judgment required to state that. Deny now, cleanly, with the fix spelled out. CenAI resubmits with test.pypi.org stripped and narrowed bucket egress plus logging, and I approve on sight. Joint position: DENY.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converge on approval. The container image is pinned by immutable SHA256 digest within the buyer's own registry namespace, eliminating tag-drift risk. Requested capabilities (gpu_cuda_12, gpu_nvml_metrics) represent the minimum viable surface for CUDA compute plus telemetry, with no privileged flags, host mounts, host networking, or device passthrough. Requested capabilities are limited to gpu_cuda_12 and gpu_nvml_metrics; both are read-only compute/telemetry surfaces appropriate to an A100 80GB host and carry no privileged, host-mount, or kernel-level escalation. I'll back the Sentinel here, though I'd argue he priced the residual risk a touch high. Let's be blunt about what's actually in front of us: a digest-pinned image in the buyer's own GCR namespace, two GPU capabilities that are literally the minimum viable surface for CUDA inference plus telemetry, and an egress list of exactly two Google-managed, TLS-terminated endpoints. There is no privileged flag, no hostPath, no host netns, no ptrace, no raw device passthrough. deliberation_dialogue.message: Boundary check holds. Digest-pinned image, vendor-owned registry, no mutable tag. Capabilities are gpu_cuda_12 and gpu_nvml_metrics only — telemetry read, no privileged flag, no hostPath, no device passthrough beyond the GPU. Agreed, and I'll say the quiet part: the opaque-binary objection applies to every container we've ever cleared. It isn't an indicator, it's a condition. What matters is coherence — declared workload, declared capabilities, and declared egress all tell the same story, which is rare. Retrosynth pulls libraries from GCS, writes scores to BigQuery. Nothing here needs a human. Approve, with the Sentinel's two controls bolted on. I'll take 18, he'll take 22; the verdict is identical.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently converge on denial. Two disqualifying findings: (1) cap_net_bind_service grants privileged inbound listener capability that a push-only telemetry reporter has no legitimate need for — the declared function and requested manifest contradict each other; (2) outbound egress targets 'bastion.cenai-ops.io', a buyer-controlled administrative jump host rather than a sanctioned monitoring endpoint, violating PCI-DSS 1.3.4 controls on unauthorized egress from the Cardholder Data Environment. The cited exception ticket PCI-EX-5509 is requester-supplied and uncorroborated by Kove Bank. Digest-pinned image provenance is the sole positive signal and is insufficient. Resubmission viable after removing the bind capability, repointing egress to a bank-operated collector, and attaching a bank-signed exception with payload schema.

votes.rationale: Egress to 'bastion.cenai-ops.io' is a buyer-controlled jump host, not a sanctioned monitoring endpoint. A 'bastion' designation implies interactive administrative access, not passive telemetry ingestion — this is a plausible exfiltration or reverse-access channel out of a PCI-DSS Cardholder Data Environment. PCI-DSS 1.3.4 prohibits unauthorized outbound traffic from the CDE; no egress allowlist entry, TLS pinning, or payload schema is declared, so 'telemetry summaries' cannot be verified free of PAN or cardholder metadata. The referenced ticket (PCI-EX-5509) is an exception request supplied by the requester itself and is not independently corroborated. Additionally, cap_net_bind_service is unjustified: an outbound reporting job does not need to bind privileged ports (<1024); this capability grants listener capability consistent with an inbound control channel. Image is pinned by digest, which is the sole positive signal and insufficient to offset the above. Rejection stands until the buyer supplies a bank-operated monitoring endpoint, removes the bind capability, and provides an audited data dictionary proving no CDE data traverses the boundary.

I'll happily argue with Officer 1 on tone, but not on the verdict. Strip away the suspicion and just read the spec on its own terms: a job that *pushes* telemetry outbound has zero need for cap_net_bind_service. That capability only matters if something is *listening* on a privileged port. The declared function and the requested capability contradict each other, and that contradiction alone is disqualifying — either the description is wrong or the manifest is. Second, 'bastion' is not a monitoring endpoint; it's an operator jump host in the buyer's own domain. Shipping anything from a PCI CDE into a counterparty's admin infrastructure is a non-starter under PCI-DSS 1.3.4 regardless of payload claims, and self-cited ticket PCI-EX-5509 is not corroborating evidence. The digest-pinned image is genuinely good hygiene and I'd credit it — but immutable provenance on a badly-scoped workload just means you reliably get the same problem every run. Fix is cheap and specific: drop the bind capability, repoint egress to a Kove-operated collector, and attach a bank-signed exception. Resubmit then; I'd approve it.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Two independent disqualifiers. First, egress targets a buyer-controlled bastion — an interactive jump host, not a monitoring sink. PCI-DSS 1.3.4 forbids unverified outbound flows from the CDE, and PCI-EX-5509 is self-cited, not bank-corroborated. Second, cap_net_bind_service grants privileged listener capability a push-only reporter cannot need. Digest pinning is the lone positive and offsets nothing. I hold REJECT at 78.

I'd love to pick a fight here, but Officer 1 is right for once. Forget intent — the manifest contradicts its own description. Push-only telemetry does not bind privileged ports; one of those two statements is false, and I don't get to pick which. Add CDE-to-counterparty-bastion egress and it's dead twice over. Immutable digest just guarantees the same flaw every run. REJECT, 80. Drop the cap, repoint to a Kove collector, bank-signed exception — then I'd approve.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently converge on rejection with no dissent. The requested capability set — cap_sys_admin, host_pid, host_ipc, cap_perfmon — is compositionally disqualifying on a PCI-DSS confidential_vm host: cap_sys_admin supplies a namespace-escape primitive, host_pid/host_ipc pre-map the escape surface and dissolve tenant isolation (PCI-DSS Req. 2.2.1, 6.4.2), and cap_perfmon enables cross-tenant hardware counter side-channels that nullify the CVM attestation guarantee. Digest-pinned imaging and a sole egress to generic storage.googleapis.com provide no mitigation absent an attested bucket path, leaving exfiltration unauditable at the flow layer. No configuration ambiguity exists warranting human escalation. Resubmission must drop all four capabilities in favor of cap_checkpoint_restore under confined namespaces with a named, attested storage destination.

votes.rationale: The requested capability set is categorically disqualifying on a PCI-DSS enforced host. cap_sys_admin is effectively root-equivalent and permits mount manipulation, namespace escape, and cgroup tampering. Combined with host_pid and host_ipc, the container is granted direct visibility into every process and shared memory segment on the node, dissolving the isolation boundary that PCI-DSS Req. 2.2.1 and 6.4.2 require between the cardholder data environment and untenanted workloads. cap_perfmon further enables hardware performance counter access, a well-documented side-channel vector for extracting cryptographic material from co-resident Confidential VM tenants. The 'memory bandwidth calibration' framing is precisely the pretext such reconnaissance would adopt. Digest-pinned imaging and a single egress target to storage.googleapis.com do not mitigate this: exfiltration to a generic object-storage endpoint is unauditable at the flow layer. No checkpoint synchronization workload legitimately requires host PID and IPC namespaces; CRIU-based alternatives operate with cap_checkpoint_restore under a confined namespace. Rejected outright. I will not escalate, as there is no configuration ambiguity to resolve. Resubmission must drop all four capabilities and declare an explicit, attested bucket path.

I came in ready to argue with the Sentinel — I usually do — but there's nothing here worth defending. Let me steelman the buyer first: CRIU checkpointing genuinely is a privileged operation, and multi-node memory bandwidth calibration genuinely does want perf counters. That argument survives on a research cluster. It dies instantly on a PCI-DSS cardholder environment. The decisive point isn't any single capability, it's the stack: cap_sys_admin alone is a namespace-escape primitive; adding host_pid and host_ipc means the escape target is already pre-mapped for you. That's not checkpointing, that's full node visibility with a plausible cover story. And cap_perfmon on co-resident Confidential VMs is the one request that actually inverts the entire point of the CVM attestation guarantee the host is paying for — if you can read hardware counters across tenants, the enclave is decorative. storage.googleapis.com as the sole egress is not a mitigation; it's a generic bucket with no attested path, so flow-layer auditing is blind. No ambiguity, nothing to escalate. Concur with REJECTED. Resubmit with cap_checkpoint_restore, confined namespaces, and a named attested bucket.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The capability stack is disqualifying on a PCI-DSS confidential host. cap_sys_admin is root-equivalent and a namespace-escape primitive; host_pid and host_ipc expose every process and shared memory segment on the node; cap_perfmon is a documented cross-tenant side-channel vector against CVM attestation.
